title: Projection on a proper/open/proper word and the graph composition tail
statement: Let A be a commutative ring and f:X→Y a scheme morphism with a supplied proper/open/proper presentation t=(a,e,p), f=a≫e≫p [def-pur-etale-graph-presentation-maps]. Define the forward graph-word projection on arbitrary unbounded M,K by the proper projection for p, Rp_* of the open tensor comparison for e, Rp_*De_! of the proper projection for a, followed by the canonical inverse pullback compositor from La*Le*Lp*K to Lf*K. For composable f,g and supplied compactifications cf,cg,ch, define the first graph presentation S=(h,e,psi≫cg.g) in the product ch.Z ×_Z cg.Z exactly as in sfGraphCompactSupportCompIso. Define its tail isomorphism by the same explicit e3 followed by the inverse graph comparison e2 for cf. Then the existing specified graph compositor is the first graph comparison followed by this tail. The data is constructed explicitly; no existence witness is selected. The transparent wrappers sfCompactProjection and sfGraphPresentationComparison display the existing projection and graph comparison at their canonical explicit functor endpoints; they introduce no mathematical data.

proof.text: Construct the product of the proper parts, its open over X and the graph h=(ch.i,f cg.i,1). Its projection to X is proper and separated, so h is proper since its composite with that projection is the identity. In the further open over Y form h′ lifting h and f; it is proper by proper-to-separated. All opens are base changes of the supplied opens.

lean.statement:
def sfGraphWordProjection
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A]
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Y} (t : EtaleGraphPresentation f)
    (M : DerivedCategoryModule A X) (K : DerivedCategoryModule A Y) :
    ((derivedTensor (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) Y).obj ((t.functor A).obj M)).obj K ⟶
      (t.functor A).obj
        (((derivedTensor (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) X).obj M).obj
          ((upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) f).leftDerivedFunctor.obj K))
lean.note: The data module explicitly constructs all three definitions and proves the compositor factorization by rfl. The lean.statement field gives the principal graph-word projection signature; the additional public declarations are the graph presentation, its tail, and the defining factorization theorem. No data is selected from a theorem with sorry.
